markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize a controlled SASRec extension testing whether recent evidence improves ranking. No improvement is established yet.

**Insights and directions.** Three baseline insights motivate intervention: causal attention does not guarantee current-purpose matching; Electronics’ 14.95% wrong-pair rate identifies weak separation; embedding similarity near 0.5 gives little evidence of severe collapse. User feedback distinguishes recent specific interests from isolated purchases, without supplying compatibility or replacement labels.

Three literature insights suggest directions: [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) separates positive calibration from negative count; [TLSTSRec](https://doi.org/10.3233/IDA-240051) motivates distinct timescales; [TransGAT](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884336/) motivates distinct relationships, although transitions cannot establish complementarity.

| Direction | Available evidence | Minimal intervention | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ranking competition | Sampled margins | Multi-negative candidate cross-entropy | False negatives; sampling objective |
| Current-interest selection | Ordered histories | Gated recent residual | Purpose remains latent |
| Relationship specificity | Titles and transitions | Separate similarity/transition scores | Compatibility unverified |

**Candidate assessments.** Scores are 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell states a strength and limitation.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: Multi-negative candidate cross-entropy [gSASRec motivation] | 3: clean comparison; established | 7: reusable; uncertain gains | 4: candidate discrimination; no recency | 8: targets separation; margins are proxies | 3: small loss change; exclusions matter |
| B: Recent residual plus A [TLSTSRec motivation] | 4: testable combination; familiar components | 7: adaptable; sparse evidence | 6: targets stale and isolated interests; specificity unverified | 8: competition; scale confounding | 5: compact branch; controls and export required |
| C: Similarity/transition residual [TransGAT motivation] | 6: distinct channels; existing fusion | 7: relational support; noisy edges | 7: specific support; no compatibility labels | 6: neighbor discrimination; popularity confounding | 7: sparse graphs; inference cost |

**Selected: B.** Add a gated mean of the last five valid prefix embeddings to SASRec. This targets stale-history influence and extrapolation from isolated older interests; it cannot establish current purpose or satisfied durable needs. Repeated occurrences contribute repeatedly, requiring a unique-ID control. Train with up to 32 distinct uniform negatives, targeting Electronics’ weak separation.

`h=SASRec(prefix); r=mean(E(last5(prefix))); z=h+sigmoid(MLP(h,r))*r; loss=CE([z·E(positive), z·E(negatives)])`.

Keep baseline normalization and √d input scaling unchanged; test added LayerNorm separately. Uncorrected candidate cross-entropy is intentional, not full-catalog sampled-softmax estimation. Corrected negatives require adding log(M/k), with the positive unchanged, for eligible-pool size M and sampled count k [sampling analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331).

Predeclare baseline, objective-only, residual-only, and combined trials. Preserve seeds, four routes, data path, predictor serialization, and diagnostic interfaces; measure the actual scorer. Stage last-item, older-window, full-history, unique-ID and normalization controls only within remaining budget. Track branch norms, gates, repeat-target strata, timestamp-gap strata, and simulator uncertainty separately from mismatch.

Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Log every validation query and cumulative charged GPU-seconds, including failures and diagnostics, within 43,200. Fix checkpoint cadence and ties beforehand. Paired category-stratified bootstrap intervals are exploratory and exclude adaptive-selection correction [Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html). Sampled HR cannot establish full-catalog quality [Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/); final generalization belongs to host evaluation.

idea.description: Extend per-dataset SASRec with a small gated recent-interest residual and uncorrected uniform multi-negative candidate cross-entropy. Compare baseline, objective-only, residual-only, and combined variants before selecting the combined model. Preserve baseline normalization in the primary comparison.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale or isolated historical purchases and broadly related recommendations lacking specific support. A recent branch explicitly targets both stale-history influence and extrapolation from isolated older interests, but cannot verify practical compatibility or immediate purpose. Multi-negative competition targets measured weak positive–negative separation, especially Electronics’ -0.4812 tenth-percentile margin and 14.95% wrong-pair rate. These are testable mechanisms rather than demonstrated gains; recent pooling may itself amplify broad similarity or recently satisfied needs.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, single-GPU execution, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Write every artifact beneath the trial directory. Retain the baseline encoder, optimizer, embedding scaling, dropout, and normalization for primary comparisons; record their resolved configurations. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps. Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores, compatibility labels, ownership, and simulator traits are unavailable regardless of illustrative schemas.

At each valid causal position, pool the last min(5, prefix_length) nonpadding item embeddings, including the current prefix endpoint and excluding future positions. Apply the shared item embedding without introducing an extra sqrt(d) factor to the residual; preserve SASRec's existing input scaling. Concatenate h and r into a scalar linear sigmoid gate, with weights initialized to zero and bias -3. Use z = h + gate*r, preserving the existing normalized h. Treat an additional output LayerNorm as a separate intervention because it changes scoring scale. Log gate distributions and branch-to-backbone norm ratios. Occurrence-weighted pooling is the primary definition; compare unique-ID pooling to detect duplicate amplification. Recent means need not favor repeated interests when all recent IDs are distinct.

For user u and positive y, define eligible negatives as real training-catalog IDs excluding all items in u's known training history and y; never consult validation or test interactions for exclusions. This matches the original training-positive exclusion proposal but defines a filtered training objective, not a causal online sampling policy. Include y exactly once as the positive even when it appears in the history. Draw k=min(32,M) unique negatives uniformly without replacement from the eligible pool of size M. Skip positions with M=0. Record exclusions and eligible-pool statistics. Unknown positives remain possible. Use temperature 1 and mean loss over valid positions; mask variable candidate padding with negative infinity. Chunk positions to bound memory. Baseline reproduction retains its original sampling; an additional matched-pool one-negative BCE control separates exclusion effects from objective effects.

Call the primary loss uncorrected candidate cross-entropy. Do not claim that uniform sampling makes positive/negative correction cancel. A separate corrected eligible-set experiment adds log(M/k) to negative logits and leaves the positive unchanged. Its partition estimate does not yield an unbiased finite-sample log-loss or gradient, and cannot recover excluded items. Exact gBCE is an optional alternative: -[beta*logsigmoid(s_pos)+sum(logsigmoid(-s_neg))]/(k+1), with beta=1-t+t*k/(N-1) under the paper's assumptions. History filtering changes those assumptions, so do not describe that beta as calibrated for the filtered pool without a new derivation. Match pools, k, temperature, and reductions for objective attribution.

Predeclare four primary variants, validation every 10 completed epochs through the configured cap, no validation-driven early stopping, and ties resolved by earlier checkpoint followed by a fixed variant order: baseline, objective-only, residual-only, combined. Enforce the shared cumulative 43,200 GPU-second limit across all slots, training, diagnostics, debugging, and failures. Use matched cumulative time caps and log incomplete runs; 200 epochs is a cap, not a substitute for compute accounting. Run optional controls only after primary comparisons and only within remaining budget. Record category HR@10, macro HR@10, every validation query, runtime, and incumbent-versus-budget traces. The host's pinned evaluator remains authoritative.

Where the host exposes per-user validation hits, retain them and bootstrap 200 users with replacement independently within each category, using identical indices across models; average the four paired category differences. Use 10,000 bootstrap replicates with a recorded analysis seed and percentile 95% intervals. One hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals condition on fixed candidates and trained models, exclude training and candidate variability, and do not correct adaptive winner selection. If hit vectors are unavailable, omit intervals rather than modifying the evaluator. Sampled HR@10 cannot establish full-catalog ranking quality.

Stage recent-window versus last-item, equally sized older-window, and full-history pooling controls; separately cross residual presence with added normalization. Report target-in-history versus unseen-target results where labels and group sizes permit without changing evaluator candidates. Timestamp-gap and repeat-frequency strata are descriptive only; never use the held-out timestamp as query time or interpret gaps as demonstrated satiation. Small strata and simulator feedback do not establish causal intent. Keep simulator users fixed and distinguish immediate choice, conditional appeal, uncertainty, and explicit mismatch. Full-catalog unseen-item recommendations cannot directly exploit repeat-ID predictions.

Serialize every architecture parameter, pooling rule, gate setting, vocabulary mapping, and checkpoint beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs the identical model, padding masks, dataset routing, and fused score. Check training/export score agreement on public training prefixes in evaluation mode. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). view.model must be the trained module; view.log2feats must return fused features and view.predict_score must use the actual scorer. Preserve model mode around probes, exclude padding, return measured metrics and definitions, and mark category breakdowns unavailable. Embedding cosine diagnostics remain descriptive and do not diagnose ranked-list diversity. Do not access hidden test files or test metrics.
idea.pseudocode:
Predeclare variants, query cadence, tie order, time caps, and optional-control order.
For each dataset, initialize the baseline with training seed 42.
For each valid training position:
  prefix = causal sequence through the current position
  h = SASRec(prefix), retaining baseline scaling and normalization
  r = mean(shared_item_embedding(last_up_to_5_valid_items(prefix)))
  gate = sigmoid(linear(concat(h, r)))  # weights=0, bias=-3 initially
  z = h + gate*r if residual_enabled else h
  eligible = real_catalog - known_user_training_items - {positive}
  k = min(32, len(eligible))
  if k == 0: skip position
  negatives = uniform_sample_without_replacement(eligible, k)
  logits = dot(z, item_embedding([positive] + negatives))
  if corrected_loss_control:
    logits[1:] += log(len(eligible)/k)
  loss = candidate_cross_entropy(logits, positive_index=0)
  # Residual-only retains baseline BCE and baseline sampling.
  # Objective-only uses h with the new candidate objective.
Mean losses over valid positions; update parameters.
Every 10 completed epochs, obtain pinned host validation and log charged time.
Stop at configured epoch cap or assigned cumulative compute cap.
Compare primary variants at matched compute; report category and macro HR@10.
Run predeclared optional controls only within remaining shared budget.
Select by macro HR@10 with fixed ties; use paired bootstrap only as exploratory evidence.
Export selected architecture and matching predictor; verify score parity.
Run adapted diagnostics through the actual fused scorer and preserve model mode.

originality.positive: A compact, falsifiable combination connects recent-history evidence with candidate competition and explicitly tests their interaction.
originality.negative: Timescale fusion, gated residuals, and multi-negative objectives are established; no novel intent-identification mechanism is demonstrated.

future_potential.positive: Controlled results could clarify when recent evidence improves heterogeneous sequential recommendation and motivate richer temporal models.
future_potential.negative: Sparse histories, sampled evaluation, and unavailable purpose or compatibility labels limit both mechanistic conclusions and transfer claims.

code_difficulty.positive: The primary model change is small and reuses SASRec embeddings, encoder, and scoring interfaces.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable causal pooling, exact negative eligibility, scale controls, budget accounting, diagnostic adaptation, and predictor parity require more work than the branch alone.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention baseline and item-dot-product scoring architecture.
Its normalization, position, residual, and embedding-scaling choices motivate preserving baseline settings during controlled comparisons.
limitations: Its ablations do not establish that a gated recent-item mean improves recency modeling.
The architecture does not establish compatibility, satisfied needs, or immediate user intent.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Studies sampled BCE overconfidence and combines generalized BCE with more negatives.
Uses independent sigmoid terms with modified positive weighting; negative count is a separate intervention.
limitations: Candidate cross-entropy is a distinct objective, not the paper's generalized BCE.
Calibration assumptions require reconsideration under user-specific history exclusions.
Reported results do not establish improvement on this pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: TLSTSRec
contributions: Combines temporal information with long- and short-term sequential modeling.
limitations: Motivates separate timescales but does not validate this five-item residual or its benchmark performance.

related_work.title: TransGAT
contributions: Models distinct complement and substitute relationships with behavioral direction.
limitations: Training transitions and textual similarity cannot supply verified complement, substitute, or compatibility labels.

related_work.title: Correcting the LogQ Correction
contributions: Explains why sampling correction must distinguish sampled negatives from the always-included positive.
Motivates explicit treatment of proposal probabilities and the target universe.
limitations: A partition estimator does not make finite-sample log-loss or gradients unbiased.
Correction cannot recover contributions from items assigned zero sampling probability.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics and reverse model orderings.
limitations: Does not change the task's required pinned sampled HR@10 objective.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit validation estimates.
Supports predeclared comparisons and cautious interpretation of selected winners.
limitations: Ordinary paired bootstrap intervals do not correct adaptive selection bias.

related_work.title: RepeatNet
contributions: Separates repeat and explore prediction mechanisms.
Motivates repeat-target stratification and occurrence-versus-unique pooling controls.
limitations: Repeat-ID prediction cannot directly improve unseen-item recommendation by recommending previously consumed IDs.
Repeated interactions do not establish present demand.

related_work.title: Scalable Demand-Aware Recommendation
contributions: Models reduced demand shortly after durable-goods purchases using category-specific replacement intervals.
limitations: Required fine-grained categories and ownership evidence are unavailable here.
Timestamp gaps alone cannot identify satiation or replacement intent.

related_work.title: Hyperparameter Optimization: Foundations, Algorithms, Best Practices, and Open Challenges
contributions: Motivates time-based search budgets and performance-versus-budget reporting.
limitations: Equal epochs do not establish equal compute, and time comparisons require matched hardware and complete accounting.

related_work.title: SciPy Bootstrap Documentation
limitations: The proposed category-stratified paired procedure must preserve category structure explicitly.
Its intervals condition on the observed models and candidates and do not address adaptive selection.
